A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same generator-induced consistency-training work despite the revised title and expanded contributions. All 14 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian simulations, training diagnostics and image-generation experiments on CIFAR-10, CelebA and ImageNet, including additional Gaussian results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic and image-generation results, including four-dataset comparisons in Table 1 and additional experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The generator-induced endpoint construction, consistency loss, EMA option and IC/GC mixing procedure are retained. Section 5.2 adds a tested variant using a separately pre-trained, frozen endpoint predictor. The change from 'coupling' to 'flows' does not itself alter the main algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 retains CIFAR-10, ImageNet at 32×32 and CelebA at 64×64, and adds LSUN Church at 64×64. It also replaces the learned 1m-2m and 2m-2m Gaussian experimental settings with a one-dimensional two-Dirac setting using a closed-form generator, substantially revising the synthetic coverage.

E2.justification: IC and batch-OT remain the main image-generation comparators, renamed iCT-IC and iCT-OT. v2 adds batch-OT to the CIFAR-10 alignment diagnostic, previously comparing IC and GC, and adds an OT panel to the CelebA qualitative comparison in Figure 7.

E3.justification: v2 adds KID and IS, equal-wall-clock and frozen-predictor controls, and coupling-specific denoisers for its revised velocity-alignment evaluation. Corresponding hyperparameter tables change minimum noise from 0.001 to 0.002 and revise learning rates, dropout settings and some network block counts. Transport evaluation also changes from intermediate-point-to-endpoint cost to noise-to-predicted-data cost; these are not interchangeable measurements.

E4.justification: v2 adds timestep-wise distribution-shift diagnostics, strong versus weak frozen endpoint predictors, dropout ablation and an equal-time control. It replaces the Gaussian gradient-variance and score-update-distance analyses with velocity-discrepancy and revised transport analyses. The optimizer/forward-process ablation disappears, fixed-step scheduling coverage narrows, and EMA analysis is reduced from three datasets to CIFAR-10.

E5.justification: v1 reports performance curves and point scores without performance uncertainty intervals. v2 introduces intervals throughout its primary FID/KID/IS table and specifies five evaluations resampling real and generated images from the same trained model. This adds systematic sampling-uncertainty reporting, not independent training-run uncertainty; the confidence level and interval calculation are unspecified.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive numerical and diagnostic results. Table 1 reports CIFAR-10 FID of 5.95 for GC, 7.42 for IC and 6.75 for OT; new LSUN results show GC trailing OT in FID, 9.88 versus 9.71. Table 2 adds equal-time and dropout results, while several earlier ablation and Gaussian result entries disappear. Revised settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: v1 contains background equations and an unscaled asymptotic-equivalence statement but no comparable theoretical development. v2 adds Theorem 1 on scaled continuous-time loss and gradient discrepancies, Theorem 2 on asymptotic velocity-estimation discrepancy, transport-cost lemmas and corollaries, and proofs in Appendix A. These introduce substantial definitions, assumptions and derivations.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims an empirically motivated coupling that accelerates training and often improves generation. v2 makes a persistent scaled continuous-time training/distillation discrepancy a central contribution and claims theoretical and empirical support for reducing that discrepancy and transport costs. Its abstract, contribution list and conclusion are substantially redefined around these claims.

C2.justification: v2 reframes GC as changing the target flow to improve velocity estimation, extending v1's interpretation of proximity to PF-ODE updates. It develops the distribution-shift explanation for GC-only failure and identifies endpoint-predictor quality as a constraint. v1's explicit lack-of-theory limitation disappears, while v2 states ideal-generator and scaling assumptions and acknowledges that GC does not fully solve alignment.

D1.justification: v2 supplements the existing implementation documentation with TorchMetrics, 50,000-image evaluation sets, resizing/cropping/scaling instructions and a Lion implementation source. Gaussian and bridge-process details are removed. Both abstracts retain the same code URL, although v2 additionally describes supplementary code and release upon publication, leaving inconsistent availability wording.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises its relationship to Song et al. by questioning the interpretation that continuous-time training closes the distillation gap. It reframes minibatch OT around approximation error and loss of the no-collision property, supported by added references including Fatras, Sommerfeld and Nurbekyan, and incorporates newer coupling work such as Li et al. These exceed bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, related-work discussion, experimental narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the discrepancy argument. Experiments are reorganized into training from scratch, frozen predictors and mixing, with numbered findings. Appendices are restructured, and the title, terminology and author information change.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the introductory schematic with probability-density and trajectory plots, replaces several diagnostic displays, and introduces a structured multi-dataset, multi-metric results table. The mixing plot narrows to CIFAR-10, while the CelebA comparison moves to the appendix and gains an OT panel. Table organization, typography, headers and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly lacked theoretical support and only hypothesized the cause of GC-only degradation. v2 adds conditional analyses and proofs, directly tests the distribution-shift explanation, and strengthens evaluation through broader metrics and an equal-time control reporting FID 6.38 versus IC's 7.42. These substantially improve the paper's explanatory and empirical support despite lost Gaussian and ablation coverage. The theory remains idealized, and reported intervals capture image-sampling rather than training variability.
